document:
Tentiles illustrated in this volume are from the collection of the University Museum and Art Gallery (UMAG), The University of Hong Kong (HKU), unless otherwise noted. UMAG's textile collection has developed over the past several decades through generous donations by individuals affiliated with the University of Hong Kong and private collectors. Several embroidery pieces were donated by Dr Hui Wai Huan, who taught in HKU's Department of Chemistry for nearly four decades, and the entire silk tapestry collection was donated by Dr Lam Kwok Pun. 
The textiles have been dated according to their weaving or embroidery techniques, use of materials, or established information on individual weavers. The comparative discussion of silk tapestry and embroidery is based on the traditional juxtaposition of these two mediums in historical texts, including catalogues of the imperial collection such as *Maidan shihui* (The Pearl from the Sea Hall) (1744), *Shi'ga haoji* (Catalogue of Painting and Calligraphy in the Qianlong Imperial Collection) (1745), and the monographs *Qing nefis ang kezi xiaotian shihua lu* (Catalogue of Kezi Silk Tapestry) *Wen'an daidi Shenhuanded Calligraphy and Painting in the Collection of the Imperial Household Department) (1930) and *Sitai biji* (Notes on Silk and Embroidery) (1933). 
Throughout the text, dimensions exclude mounts or frames; height precedes width. Chinese names are given in the traditional order, surname first. The transliteration of Chinese names, places and techniques into English follows the Pinyin system of romanisation. Chinese terms are italicised unless commonly used in English.
